messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING oncall: trace-exporter error rate >6% to NewRelic EU ingest (observability). Severity: P2. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tracing-exporters

jake: ack, looking. I see repeated 503 and connection resets from newrelic exporter in otel-collector logs starting ~18:07 UTC.

rachel: metrics show span ingestion drop for eu-west-1 services. dashboards: https://grafana.internal/d/abcd/traces?from=now-1h

infra: can we enable disk-buffering and switch to a durable sink while NR is flaky? we have GCS backup configured.

jake: yes. propose: 1) set EXPORT_BACKENDS=gcs,newrelic 2) enable file_buffer in collector (10GB) 3) reduce sampling from 100% -> 20% for high-volume services 4) open NR support ticket.

maria: I can patch the collector config. commands: `kubectl -n observability set env deploy/otel-collector EXPORT_BACKENDS=gcs,newrelic && kubectl -n observability set env deploy/otel-collector FILE_BUFFER_ENABLED=true && kubectl -n observability set env deploy/otel-collector TRACE_SAMPLE_RATE=0.2`

jake: apply when ready. also add `OTEL_EXPORTER_RETRY_ON_FAILURE=on` so retries are buffered to disk.

(oncall-bot): User jake acknowledged the page at 18:10 UTC

maria: applying now, rolling update. watching pod logs.

rachel: logs show initial 503s: ```
2026-11-02T18:07:23Z warn exporter/newrelic send failed: status=503 body="Service Unavailable"
2026-11-02T18:07:24Z error exporter/newrelic connection reset by peer
2026-11-02T18:08:01Z warn exporter/newrelic throttled: status=429 body="rate limit exceeded"
```

infra: newrelic status page shows incident in EU region: https://status.newrelic.com/incidents/NR-20261102-77

newrelic-support-bot: Support ticket created: NR-20261102-77. Assigned to Engineering. Latest: investigating ingress throttling in EU.

jake: great. mitigation in place: collector now buffering to disk + GCS fallback. sampling reduced. verifying traffic out to GCS.

maria: `kubectl -n observability logs deploy/otel-collector --since=10m | grep PUT | tail -n 5` shows successful uploads to gcs-bucket: `PUT https://storage.googleapis.com/redwood-traces/ 200`

rachel: customer impact assessment: traces delayed/missing for ~18:07-18:25 UTC for EU-hosted services. No API or customer request impact. this is observability-only. drafting customer note.

jake: write short notice: "We observed delayed and dropped traces to New Relic EU between 18:0718:25 UTC due to a vendor ingest issue. We have enabled local buffering and rerouted traces to our GCS backup to ensure durability; we will replay buffered data to New Relic when the vendor is healthy. Application traffic not impacted." link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1766633333/notice

(oncall-bot): Incident severity lowered to P3 at 18:22 UTC after mitigations applied.

infra: starting backfill worker to replay buffered traces from disk -> GCS. backfill job id: backfill-1766633333-1. monitor at https://internal.jobs/backfill/backfill-1766633333-1

maria: handing off monitoring to night oncall @maria until 02:00 UTC. see runbook step 5 for backfill and validation: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tracing-exporters#backfill

jake: filing internal incident ticket REN-INC-4887, attaching exporter logs and NR ticket link.

newrelic-support-bot: Update from New Relic: "We are seeing ingress rate limiting in EU ingest due to a configuration rollout; mitigation in progress. Customers may see delayed spans; full recovery TBD."

rachel: will monitor for backfill completion and confirm with New Relic when they finish. will post update to #general and customers channel.

maria: ack. monitoring gcs queue and disk buffer size. if disk buffer >80% or GCS fails, escalate to infra immediately.

(oncall-bot): Incident closed (mitigated) at 18:45 UTC - monitoring handoff to maria for backfill. Postmortem owner: rachel.
